findings.title: Materials' 67-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at a 67-point percentile gap between trailing (89) and forward (23) valuations, the widest in the table. The market is pricing 118 percent earnings growth that would cut the forward multiple to 16.23x — a bet on a profit rebound so steep it looks like a cyclical trough call.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' 50-point gap after 29-point weekly drop
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile fell 29 points in one week to 42, while trailing sits at 92 — a 50-point split. That collapse is not a valuation story but a re-rating: analysts now expect 53 percent earnings growth, and the market is refusing to pay up for it.

findings.title: Energy's forward discount despite 56 percent growth
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E of 12.06 sits at percentile 47 while trailing is at 82, a 34-point gap favoring the trailing lens. The market is underwriting 56 percent earnings growth yet still prices the sector below its five-year median forward multiple — a skepticism that growth will actually materialize.
